turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a little lost but gathered his courage and walked towards the door, nodding to Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the boy walk towards the door with a mix of curiosity and disdain. She called out to him, telling Pip to wait just a moment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip nodded and stood there, waiting just as Miss Havisham had asked, feeling a bit like a statue in the silent room.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the boy intently, her eyes lingering on the young face before she spoke in a commanding tone, telling Pip to go and fetch Estella now.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip nodded again, feeling a bit more uneasy as he wondered where Estella was and what she looked like, but he walked towards the door to do as Miss Havisham had asked.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip leave, her eyes narrowing as if she were weighing some unseen measure. She then called out sharply, telling the boy to return once he had located Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip was a bit relieved to be given an errand, and he hoped that finding Estella wouldn’t take too long.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched Pip's back as he disappeared through the door, her gaze turning to the dusty windows and the stopped clocks around her room. She sighed deeply, a mix of bitterness and anticipation settling over her.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his way down the dark corridor, wondering where Estella might be and if she would be as strange as Miss Havisham had hinted.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes flickered with a mix of curiosity and disdain as she waited for Pip to return with Estella. She was eager to see how the boy would react to her protégée.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip moved cautiously down the dimly lit hallway, his heart pounding with each creak of the floorboards. He hoped he wouldn't run into anything or anyone else, and wondered how long it would take to find Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham watched the boy's progress, her eyes narrowing with a mixture of curiosity and something like amusement. She leaned forward, her hand gripping the edge of the chair as if she was ready to spring into action at any moment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt a shiver run down his spine as he neared the appointed room, his breath catching in his throat as he wondered what Miss Havisham would do next.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: She was impatient now, tapping her fingers against the arm of the chair, her eyes fixed on the door through which Pip had disappeared. She wondered what the boy would think of Estella, how he would react to her protégée’s coldness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt the weight of the silence and the heavy atmosphere as he stood in front of the door, his hand hovering over the handle.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes glinted with a strange intensity as she waited for Pip to reappear, her fingers tapping out an impatient rhythm on the arm of her chair.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip turned the handle slowly, his heart pounding in his chest, and stepped into the room, his eyes immediately seeking Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes flickered to Pip as he entered the room, her lips curling into a cold smile. She motioned for him to approach, her voice as sharp as a blade when she spoke.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Pip felt his knees buckle slightly as Miss Havisham’s cold smile sent a shiver down his spine. He took a deep breath and stepped closer to her, his voice barely above a whisper as he spoke to her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Miss Havisham's eyes narrowed as she observed Pip's nervousness, her voice as cold and sharp as the autumn wind when she spoke, commanding him to tell her about his life.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Pip, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Pip?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip informed Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer; let her look at him. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was not afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched here?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he did, ma’am.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip what she touched?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that it was broken!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired. She wanted diversion, and she had done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies, and she had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was not, ma’am, he was very sorry for her, and very sorry he could not play just now. If she complained of him he would get into trouble with his sister, so he would do it if he could; but it was so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham remarked that it was so new to him, so old to her; so strange to him, so familiar to her; so melancholy to both of them! She asked Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella. At the door.
